method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child' (last update September 2022, PIC endorsed), 55 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at https://www.rch.org.au/ (Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'RCH flowcharts for Febrile child' (two management flowcharts on the same page (image files dated Feb 2025), transcribed in Wave 1), 9 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at https://www.rch.org.au/ (Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the hand-written Wave 1 page (which quoted RCH) as a paraphrase. Every Wave 1 claim is carried over and re-anchored in the page as fetched on 2026-09-24, one in part (see Unresolved), and one claim on the page's age tiers is added so the flowchart claims can be placed by age. S2 anchors point into a text transcription of the two flowcharts made in Wave 1; the flowcharts are images and were not re-read.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Febrile neonate (28 days or under, corrected):** investigate (FBE, CRP, cultures of blood, urine and CSF, ± chest X-ray) and start empiric IV antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Febrile infant over 28 days and under 3 months (corrected):** investigate and treat readily, guided by how the infant looks and whether an obvious focus is present.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Under 3 months, low or unstable temperature** can signal serious bacterial infection or other serious illness.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fever height, speed of onset, response to antipyretics and febrile seizures do not predict severity;** the child's appearance is the most useful sign.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Fever:** body temperature above 38.0º Celsius.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Measure consistently:** the same site and the same kind of thermometer each time, where you can.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Most fevers are viral,** but serious bacterial infection (SBI) must be considered; without a focus, the commonest SBI is a urinary tract infection.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Occult bacteraemia** is now under 1% in healthy, immunised children, since pneumococcal vaccination began.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Fever for 5 days or more:** assess for Kawasaki disease, or PIMS-TS if the child has had COVID-19.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Prolonged fever** can also come from rarer inflammatory, immune-mediated or malignant conditions, which may need a specialist.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Ask about localising symptoms:** cough · headache · light sensitivity · vomiting · diarrhoea · tummy pain · muscle or joint pain · rash.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Antibiotics already given** can hide the signs of a bacterial infection.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **High-risk groups:** prematurity · immunosuppression or cancer (see febrile neutropenia) · a central line · chronic lung disease · congenital heart disease · a past invasive bacterial infection · Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander, Pacific Islander or Māori children · repeated presentations to health services.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Teething is not a cause of fever.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Fever after vaccination** is common, usually starting within 24 hours and lasting up to 2-3 days. ⚠️ If the child is unwell, do not put the fever down to the vaccine alone.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Behaviour and appearance** are the best guide to whether a child is at high risk of SBI.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Colour:** pallor (including when a parent reports it) · mottling · blue or cyanosed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Activity:** lethargic or less active · not responding normally to social cues · hard to wake, or will not stay awake once roused · a weak, high-pitched or continuous cry.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Breathing:** grunting · tachypnoea · increased work of breathing · hypoxia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Circulation and hydration:** feeding poorly · dry mucous membranes · tachycardia that persists · central capillary refill 3 seconds or longer · reduced skin turgor · passing less urine.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Neurological:** a bulging fontanelle · neck stiffness · marked irritability · focal neurological signs · seizures that are focal, complex or prolonged.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Other:** a rash that does not blanch · fever for 5 days or more · a swollen limb or joint · not bearing weight or not using a limb.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **These signs are adapted** from the 2019 NICE guideline on feverish illness in children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Examine for a focus of infection,** undressing the child as needed for a complete examination and looking for subtle signs.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A febrile child who looks seriously unwell is managed as suspected sepsis,** however high or low the temperature.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not accept an apparent otitis media or cold as the source** in a young infant or an unwell child; they still need assessing for SBI.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Stable child:** preferably finish the search for a focus before starting antibiotics. High-risk groups: investigate more readily.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **UTI is the commonest SBI:** with no obvious focus, collect and test urine.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Antibiotic choice** depends on local susceptibility patterns; use local guidelines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Three corrected-age tiers:** 28 days or under · 29 days to 3 months · over 3 months. The two flowcharts below cover the older two tiers.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Assess quickly for sepsis and involve a senior doctor.** Do FBE, CRP, blood culture, urine (by suprapubic aspirate, SPA; other methods below), LP ± chest X-ray, and treat promptly with empiric antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not wait for the full work-up** if the infant looks unwell or the investigations will be delayed: give the antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Start point:** temperature above 38.0 C. First branch: unwell features or not. Second branch: an obvious clinical focus or not.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Febrile child', two management flowcharts on the same page (image files dated Feb 2025), transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_29%20day%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_3%20month%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Unwell with signs of septic shock:** follow the sepsis guideline.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Febrile child', two management flowcharts on the same page (image files dated Feb 2025), transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_29%20day%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_3%20month%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Empiric antibiotic:** ceftriaxone, or cefazolin plus gentamicin once CSF is normal or meningitis has been excluded; check local antimicrobial guidelines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Febrile child', two management flowcharts on the same page (image files dated Feb 2025), transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_29%20day%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_3%20month%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Well, obvious focus:** investigate and treat according to the focus; if sending home, arrange review within 12-24 h.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Febrile child', two management flowcharts on the same page (image files dated Feb 2025), transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_29%20day%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_3%20month%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Well, no focus:** urine MCS (SPA or catheter), and consider FBE, CRP and blood culture; consider admitting for observation and senior review. Still well with normal results → home with review in 12-24 h. Positive urine → see the UTI guideline.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Febrile child', two management flowcharts on the same page (image files dated Feb 2025), transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_29%20day%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_3%20month%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Unwell, obvious focus:** investigate and treat the focus, look for co-infection or complications, admit, and treat as the clinical picture requires.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Febrile child', two management flowcharts on the same page (image files dated Feb 2025), transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_29%20day%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_3%20month%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Unwell, no focus:** FBE, BSL, lactate, baseline CRP, blood culture, urine MCS, ⚠️ LP unless contraindicated, ± chest X-ray; admit.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Febrile child', two management flowcharts on the same page (image files dated Feb 2025), transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_29%20day%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_3%20month%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Well, no focus:** fever under 24 h → consider no tests. Previous UTI, or age under 12 months with fever over 24 h → consider urine MCS. Fever over 48 h → consider urine MCS at any age and discuss further tests with a senior doctor. Home with review within 24 h.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Febrile child', two management flowcharts on the same page (image files dated Feb 2025), transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_29%20day%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_3%20month%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Unwell, no focus:** FBE, BSL, lactate, baseline CRP, blood culture, urine MCS, ± LP, ± chest X-ray; admit.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Febrile child', two management flowcharts on the same page (image files dated Feb 2025), transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_29%20day%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/charts/Febrile%20child%20CPG_3%20month%20plus%20flowchart_Feb2025.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Talk to the local paediatric team** for: an unwell child · septic shock · any infant under 28 days corrected with fever (admit for empiric antibiotics) · social or other barriers to review within 24 hours (consider admitting) · a high-risk child · advice on empiric treatment · prolonged fever without a clear cause.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Transfer to a tertiary centre** if the child needs more care than the local hospital is comfortable giving.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Discharge:** 29 days to 3 months corrected, when well, results normal, a senior doctor has been consulted and review in 12-24 hours is booked. Over 3 months corrected, when well and follow-up is arranged.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Always tell parents** to come back if the child gets worse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Axillary** is advised under 3 months; hold the thermometer over the axillary artery for 3 minutes for a more accurate reading.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Tympanic** is advised over 3 months; pull the pinna back to straighten the ear canal and aim the probe at the eardrum.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Forehead and infrared skin thermometers are unreliable.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Rectal (neonates):** screen with an axillary reading first; take a rectal temperature only if fever is still suspected.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **When an LP is indicated, do it promptly,** ideally before antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not do an LP** with impaired consciousness, focal neurological signs, a coagulation problem or haemodynamic instability.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **If an LP is contraindicated,** start treatment for meningitis or encephalitis and do the LP later, once the child is stable and it is safe.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never culture a bag specimen:** half are contaminated (50%), giving false positives.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Suprapubic aspirate** is the gold standard (1% contamination). **In/out catheter** helps when the bladder holds little urine, e.g. after a failed clean catch or SPA; discard the first drops if possible (10% contamination).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Midstream urine** is preferred in toilet-trained children who can pass urine on request (25% contamination). **Clean catch** suits pre-continent children who cannot, provided they are not seriously unwell (also 25%).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Before a midstream or clean-catch sample,** clean the genital area with saline-soaked gauze for 10 seconds.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Take blood cultures aseptically, in sterile gloves.** Results are only as good as the volume collected; if there is not enough for both bottles, fill the aerobic one first.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Bottle limits:** paediatric aerobic, 0.5 mL minimum to 4 mL maximum; adult aerobic, 5 mL minimum to 10 mL maximum.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Volume by weight** (paediatric aerobic bottle, then adult aerobic): under 1.5 kg, 1 mL, adult bottle not used unless specifically indicated · 1.5 mL for 1.5-5 kg · 5-10 kg, paediatric 3 mL or adult 5 mL · 11-15 kg, paediatric 4 mL or adult 5 mL.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Heavier children:** 16-20 kg, 6 mL adult aerobic and 6 mL anaerobic (use the green bottle whenever more than 4 mL is collected; with no anaerobic culture, put 10 mL in the aerobic bottle) · 21-25 kg, 8 mL each · over 25 kg, 10 mL each.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Currency:** the page states its last update as September 2022.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **PIC endorsed.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Largest study cited:** Craig et al., BMJ 2010, a prospective cohort of 15 781 febrile illnesses testing how accurately symptoms and signs diagnose SBI in young children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Also cited:** a systematic review finding infrared ear thermometers insensitive for fever in children (Dodd et al.), and the validation of the Step-by-Step approach to young febrile infants (Gomez et al., 2016).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile child', last update September 2022, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/febrile_child/, retrieved 2026-09-24
